intro: 100 questions covering all A1, A2 and B1 grammar and vocabulary. Questions are in English with Croatian examples. Take your time — there is no time limit.

questions.prompt: Which greeting is used in the morning?
questions.explanation: Dobro jutro means Good morning and is used until around noon.

questions.prompt: How do you say goodbye formally in Croatian?
questions.explanation: Doviđenja is the formal farewell, equivalent to Goodbye. Bok and Čao are informal.

questions.prompt: How do you say 17 in Croatian?
questions.explanation: 17 = sedamnaest. The -naest suffix corresponds to English -teen.

questions.prompt: Complete: Imam ___ godina. (I am 25 years old.)
questions.explanation: Imam dvadeset i pet godina. Numbers above 20 are formed with i (and) between tens and units.

questions.prompt: Koliko je sati? The clock shows 3:00. What is the correct answer?
questions.explanation: Tri su sata — with 3 (tri) the verb is su (are) and sat takes the genitive plural form sata.

questions.prompt: What does ponedjeljak mean?
questions.explanation: Ponedjeljak = Monday. The days: ponedjeljak, utorak, srijeda, četvrtak, petak, subota, nedjelja.

questions.prompt: Which adjective form is correct? ___ auto (a red car — auto is masculine)
questions.explanation: Auto is masculine. The base form of the adjective (indefinite) for masculine is crven. Crvena is feminine, crveno is neuter.

questions.prompt: What is the Croatian word for grandmother?
questions.explanation: Baka = grandmother. Majka = mother, sestra = sister, teta = aunt.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive: ___ brat (my brother)
questions.explanation: Brat is masculine singular, so the possessive adjective moj is used (masculine form). Moja is feminine, moje is neuter.

questions.prompt: What does kruh mean?
questions.explanation: Kruh = bread. Mlijeko = milk, voda = water, sir = cheese.

questions.prompt: Complete: Volim ___ kavu. (I like coffee.)
questions.explanation: Kava (coffee) is a drink, so the verb is piti (to drink). Pojesti = to eat up, gledati = to watch.

questions.prompt: Complete: Mi ___ u Zagrebu. (We live in Zagreb.)
questions.explanation: Mi = we. The verb živjeti (to live) conjugates: ja živim, ti živiš, on/ona živi, mi živimo, vi živite, oni žive.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ana ___ glazbu svaki dan. (Ana listens to music every day.)
questions.explanation: Ana is 3rd person singular. Slušati (-ati verb): ja slušam, ti slušaš, on/ona sluša.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ja ___ student. (I am a student.)
questions.explanation: Biti (to be): ja sam, ti si, on/ona/ono je, mi smo, vi ste, oni su.

questions.prompt: What gender is the noun auto (car)?
questions.explanation: Auto is masculine. In Croatian, nouns ending in a consonant are usually masculine.

questions.prompt: What is the plural of grad (city)?
questions.explanation: Most masculine nouns form their plural with -ovi: grad → gradovi. Some short masculines take -evi.

questions.prompt: Complete: Knjižnica ___ blizu škole. (The library is near the school.)
questions.explanation: Knjižnica is feminine singular, so biti = je (3rd person singular).

questions.prompt: Complete: Idem ___ školu. (I am going to school.)
questions.explanation: For going into an enclosed institution, Croatian uses u + accusative: u školu. Na is used for open spaces or events.

questions.prompt: What is the Croatian word for kitchen?
questions.explanation: Kuhinja = kitchen. Soba = room, kupaonica = bathroom, hodnik = corridor.

questions.prompt: How do you say It is raining in Croatian?
questions.explanation: Pada kiša literally means Rain is falling. This is the standard expression for It is raining.

questions.prompt: Complete: Volim ___ knjige. (I love reading books.)
questions.explanation: Čitati = to read. Pisati = to write, plivati = to swim, kuhati = to cook.

questions.prompt: Which word means tram?
questions.explanation: Tramvaj = tram. Vlak = train, autobus = bus, brod = boat/ship.

questions.prompt: Complete: Petra se ___ u sedam ujutro. (Petra wakes up at seven in the morning.)
questions.explanation: Buditi se is reflexive. 3rd person singular: on/ona se budi. Budim is 1st person (ja se budim).

questions.prompt: What does večerati mean?
questions.explanation: Večerati = to have dinner (večera = dinner/supper). Doručkovati = breakfast, ručati = lunch.

questions.prompt: How do you say I do not have in Croatian?
questions.explanation: The negative of imati is nemam (ne + am contracted). Ne imam is not standard; nemam is the correct form.

questions.prompt: Complete: On ___ u Dubrovnik prošle godine. (He went to Dubrovnik last year.)
questions.explanation: Past tense (perfekt): auxiliary je + past participle. On (he, masculine) → otišao je. Otišla je would be feminine (she).

questions.prompt: Complete: Marija ___ cijelu noć. (Marija studied all night.)
questions.explanation: Marija is feminine. Past participle of učiti: učio (m), učila (f), učilo (n). So: Marija je učila.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct past tense of biti for ja (I, male)?
questions.explanation: Ja + masculine → bio sam (I was). Female speaker: bila sam. Bio je = he was.

questions.prompt: Complete: Mi ___ na moru prošlo ljeto. (We were at the sea last summer.)
questions.explanation: Mi smo bili (or bili smo) is the past of biti for we (mixed or male group). Clitic: smo moves to second position.

questions.prompt: What is the past participle of ići (to go)?
questions.explanation: Ići has the irregular past participle: išao (masculine), išla (feminine), išlo (neuter).

questions.prompt: Complete: Ja ___ sutra u Split. (I will go to Split tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: Futur I = ću/ćeš/će... + infinitive. Ja ću ići (or short form: Ići ću). The short clitic ću follows the infinitive in everyday speech.

questions.prompt: Complete: Oni ___ na večeru. (They will eat dinner.)
questions.explanation: Oni (they) → će (3rd person plural future clitic). Će večerati.

questions.prompt: What is the correct future form of ti (you, singular)?
questions.explanation: Future clitics: ja ću, ti ćeš, on/ona će, mi ćemo, vi ćete, oni će.

questions.prompt: Complete: Hoćemo li ___ na kavu? (Shall we go for a coffee?)
questions.explanation: Hoćemo li + infinitive is used for Shall we...? The infinitive ići is used after modal/auxiliary verbs.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: Vidim ___ (brat — brother, animate masculine).
questions.explanation: Animate masculine nouns take -a in the accusative: brat → brata. Inanimate masculines stay the same.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: Kupujem ___ (knjiga — book, feminine).
questions.explanation: Feminine -a nouns change to -u in the accusative: knjiga → knjigu.

questions.prompt: Complete: Idem ___ grad. (I am going into the city — movement.)
questions.explanation: For movement toward a place (into), Croatian uses u + accusative. U gradu (locative) = in the city; u grad (accusative) = into the city.

questions.prompt: Which noun does NOT change in the accusative?
questions.explanation: Neuter nouns are identical in nominative and accusative: more stays more. Feminine -a nouns change to -u; animate masculine takes -a.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dao sam poklon ___. (I gave a gift to my sister.)
questions.explanation: The indirect object (recipient) takes the dative. Sestra (feminine -a) → sestri in dative.

questions.prompt: Complete: ___ mi se sviđa Zagreb. (I like Zagreb — lit. Zagreb appeals to me.)
questions.explanation: Sviđati se governs the dative. Mi = dative of ja. With singular subject (Zagreb): sviđa mi se.

questions.prompt: What does Hladno mi je mean?
questions.explanation: Hladno mi je = It is cold to me = I am cold. Mi is the dative of ja. This is an impersonal dative expression.

questions.prompt: How do you ask How much does it cost?
questions.explanation: Koliko košta? = How much does it cost? Koliko je sati = What time is it? Gdje je kasa = Where is the till?

questions.prompt: What does haljina mean?
questions.explanation: Haljina = dress. Kaput = coat, hlače = trousers, cipela = shoe.

questions.prompt: Complete: ___ me glava. (I have a headache — My head hurts.)
questions.explanation: Boljeti works like sviđati se: glava (singular subject) → boli. Bole is used with plural subjects (e.g. noge me bole).

questions.prompt: What does liječnik mean?
questions.explanation: Liječnik = doctor (male). Liječnica = female doctor. Medicinska sestra = nurse, zubar = dentist.

questions.prompt: Which adjective is the feminine form of visok (tall)?
questions.explanation: Adjective agreement in Croatian: masculine = visok, feminine = visoka, neuter = visoko.

questions.prompt: How do you say She has blue eyes in Croatian?
questions.explanation: Imati is used for physical features: Ona ima plave oči. Oči (eyes) is plural feminine → plave (accusative plural feminine).

questions.prompt: Complete: Moram ___ u devet sati. (I must be at work at nine.)
questions.explanation: Morati (must) is followed by the infinitive: moram biti (I must be). Modal verbs always take infinitive.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ne mogu ___ sutra. (I cannot come tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: Moći (can) takes the infinitive: ne mogu doći. After moći, use the infinitive form doći, not the subjunctive or imperative.

questions.prompt: Which verb means should / ought to?
questions.explanation: Trebati = to need / should. Trebao bi (m) / trebala bi (f) = he/she should. Morati = must, moći = can, htjeti = to want.

questions.prompt: What is the comparative of dobar (good)?
questions.explanation: Dobar has an irregular comparative: bolji (better). Its superlative is najbolji.

questions.prompt: Complete: Zagreb je ___ od Osijeka. (Zagreb is bigger than Osijek.)
questions.explanation: The comparative of velik (big) is veći. Superlative: najveći. The regular comparative adds -iji but velik has a special form.

questions.prompt: How do you say the most beautiful in Croatian?
questions.explanation: Superlatives are formed with naj- prefix: lijep → ljepši (comparative) → najljepši (superlative).

questions.prompt: What does Što kažeš da idemo na večeru? mean?
options: What do you say we go for dinner?
questions.explanation: Što kažeš da... = What do you say if/that we...? It is a casual suggestion structure used to propose doing something together.

questions.prompt: Complete: ___ li idemo na koncert? (Shall we go to the concert?)
questions.explanation: Hoćemo li = Shall we? / Do we want to? It is the 1st person plural (we) question form of htjeti.

questions.prompt: Complete: To je kuća moje ___. (That is my mother's house.)
questions.explanation: Possession uses the genitive. Majka (feminine -a) → majke in genitive. Moje is the genitive of moja (feminine possessive).

questions.prompt: Which preposition requires the genitive case?
questions.explanation: Zbog (because of) always takes the genitive. U and na take accusative (movement) or locative (location). S/sa takes the instrumental.

questions.prompt: Complete: Nemam ___. (I have no time.)
questions.explanation: Negated direct objects often take the genitive in Croatian. Nema + genitive, nemam + genitive: nemam vremena.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kako se ___ ? (What is your name? — lit. What are you called?)
questions.explanation: Zvati se = to be called. 2nd person: Kako se zoveš? The particle se can come before or after the verb but is part of the verb.

questions.prompt: What does osjećati se mean?
questions.explanation: Osjećati se = to feel (how one feels). Osjećam se dobro = I feel well. The se makes it reflexive (to feel oneself).

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a completed, one-time past action?
questions.explanation: Pročitao sam roman uses the perfective verb pročitati — the novel is fully read. Čitao sam (imperfective) would describe ongoing or repeated reading.

questions.prompt: Which verb is imperfective?
questions.explanation: Pisati (to write, ongoing) is imperfective. Napisati (to write — completed) is perfective. In general, prefixed verbs tend to be perfective.

questions.prompt: Complete: Svako jutro ___ kavu. (Every morning I drink coffee — habitual.)
questions.explanation: Habitual/repeated actions use the imperfective present: pijem (I drink — regularly). Popijem would suggest each time I finish a coffee.

questions.prompt: Which is the perfective partner of gledati (to watch)?
questions.explanation: Pogledati (to take a look / to watch — completed) is the standard perfective partner of gledati.

questions.prompt: The present tense in Croatian always uses which aspect?
questions.explanation: The Croatian present tense always uses imperfective verbs. A perfective verb in the present tense expresses a future meaning (e.g. Donesem ti to = I will bring that to you).

questions.prompt: Complete: Idem ___ prijateljem u kino. (I am going to the cinema with my friend.)
questions.explanation: Accompaniment uses s/sa + instrumental: s prijateljem (with my friend). Prijatelj (masculine) → prijateljem in instrumental.

questions.prompt: Complete: Putujemo ___. (We are travelling by train.)
questions.explanation: Transport without a preposition uses the instrumental: vlak → vlakom. This is a key use of the instrumental case.

questions.prompt: What is the instrumental singular of žena (woman, feminine -a noun)?
questions.explanation: Feminine -a nouns form the instrumental with -om: žena → ženom. Hard masculine/neuter nouns also take -om; soft stems take -em.

questions.prompt: Complete: Živim ___ gradu. (I live in the city.)
questions.explanation: For being inside a city or enclosed space, Croatian uses u + locative: u gradu.

questions.prompt: What happens to k when grad (city) takes the locative ending -u?
questions.explanation: Velar softening before locative -u: k → c, g → z, h → s. So grad does not change because it ends in d, not k. But vojnik → vojniku... Actually grad → gradu (d stays). Example of k→c: junak → junaku (no, junak → junaci...). Correct: vojnik → vojniku? Actually k→c in locative: rijek → rijeci. The most common: tjedan → tjednu; ruka (f) → ruci. For masculine: k→c is seen. Majority answer: k becomes c.

The velar k softens to c before locative -u in certain nouns: e.g. vojnik → u vojniku (short masc), or in feminine: ruka → ruci. In masculine singular locative, k remains as k before -u in most modern usage, but female nouns with k soften to c. The principle is: k → c.

questions.prompt: Which preposition uses the locative to mean about (a topic)?
questions.explanation: O + locative = about: Govorimo o poslu = We are talking about work. Za takes accusative, od takes genitive, s/sa takes instrumental.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ja ___ htio ostati dulje. (I would have liked to stay longer — male speaker.)
questions.explanation: The conditional clitics: ja bih, ti bi, on/ona/ono bi, mi bismo, vi biste, oni bi. Ja = bih.

questions.prompt: Which form expresses a polite request to a group?
questions.explanation: Biste li mogli...? = Could you (plural/formal) ...? It is the standard polite request form. Bi li mogao = Could he / Could you (informal sg)?

questions.prompt: Complete: Kad bih imao more novca, ___ u inozemstvo. (If I had more money, I would move abroad.)
questions.explanation: Type 2 conditional (hypothetical): Kad bih + past tense... then past participle + bih/bi etc. Otišao bih = I would go (male speaker).

questions.prompt: What is the negative conditional for we?
questions.explanation: Negative conditional: ne bih (I), ne bi (you sg / he/she), ne bismo (we), ne biste (you pl), ne bi (they).

questions.prompt: Complete: Čovjek ___ ovdje radi je moj brat. (The man who works here is my brother.)
questions.explanation: Koji/koja/koje agrees with the antecedent in gender and number. Čovjek is masculine singular → koji. It is in the nominative because it is the subject of radi.

questions.prompt: Complete: Knjiga ___ čitam je zanimljiva. (The book that I am reading is interesting.)
questions.explanation: Knjiga is feminine. In the relative clause, the book is the direct object of čitam → accusative. Feminine accusative of koji = koju.

questions.prompt: What does čiji mean?
questions.explanation: Čiji/čija/čije = whose. It shows possession: Prijatelj čiji brat živi u Londonu = The friend whose brother lives in London.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct conjunction: Mislim ___ je to dobra ideja. (I think that is a good idea.)
questions.explanation: Misliti (to think/believe) takes da: Mislim da je to dobra ideja. Što is used after verbs of emotion/feeling (Drago mi je što si tu).

questions.prompt: Complete: Drago mi je ___ si došao. (I am glad that you came.)
questions.explanation: After verbs and expressions of emotion (drago mi je, žao mi je, veseli me), Croatian uses što, not da.

questions.prompt: What does iako mean?
questions.explanation: Iako = although / even though. Jer = because, ako = if, dok = while.

questions.prompt: What is the passive participle of napisati (to write)?
questions.explanation: Passive participles of -ati verbs take -an/-ana/-ano: napisati → napisan (m), napisana (f), napisano (n).

questions.prompt: Complete: Ovdje se ___ engleski. (English is spoken here — se-passive.)
questions.explanation: Se-passive with a singular subject (engleski) takes the 3rd person singular: Ovdje se govori engleski.

questions.prompt: Complete: Film je ___ u Dubrovniku. (The film was shot in Dubrovnik.)
questions.explanation: Biti-passive: je + passive participle. Film is masculine singular → snimljen (passive participle of snimiti).

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said: I am tired. → He said that ___.
questions.explanation: Indirect statements in Croatian use da + the original tense (no backshift). He said that he is tired → Rekao je da je umoran.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct indirect yes/no question: She asked: Is he at home? → She asked ___.
options: da li je on kod kuće
questions.explanation: Indirect yes/no questions use je li or da li: Pitala je je li on kod kuće / Pitala je da li je on kod kuće.

questions.prompt: Convert: She told me: Come home! → She told me ___ home.
questions.explanation: Indirect commands use da + present tense: Rekla mi je da idem kući. The present tense (idem) is used, not the imperative (idi).

questions.prompt: What does životopis mean?
questions.explanation: Životopis = CV (curriculum vitae / résumé). Razgovor za posao = job interview, oglas za posao = job advertisement, ugovor o radu = work contract.

questions.prompt: What does šef/šefica mean?
questions.explanation: Šef (m) / šefica (f) = boss. Kolega/kolegica = colleague, zaposlenik = employee, klijent = client.

questions.prompt: What does preuzeti mean in the context of technology?
questions.explanation: Preuzeti = to download. Učitati = to upload, prijaviti se = to log in, obrisati = to delete.

questions.prompt: What does društvene mreže mean?
questions.explanation: Društvene mreže = social networks / social media. Vijesti = news, streaming platforma = streaming service.

questions.prompt: Complete: Brinem se ___ klimatskih promjena. (I am worried about climate change.)
questions.explanation: Brinuti se zbog + genitive = to worry because of / about. Zbog requires the genitive case.

questions.prompt: Which Croatian national park is famous for its lakes and waterfalls?
questions.explanation: Plitvička jezera (Plitvice Lakes) is Croatia's most famous national park, known for its terraced lakes and waterfalls. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.prompt: Complete: Trebao ___ više spavati. (He should sleep more.)
questions.explanation: Trebati in the conditional: on (he) → trebao bi (he should). Female: trebala bi. This is advice using the conditional.

questions.prompt: What does uravnotežena prehrana mean?
questions.explanation: Uravnotežena prehrana = balanced diet. Intenzivno vježbanje = intensive exercise, mentalno zdravlje = mental health, dobar san = good sleep.

questions.prompt: In which year did Croatia declare independence?
questions.explanation: Croatia declared independence in 1991 (Hrvatska je proglasila neovisnost 1991. godine).

questions.prompt: In which year did Croatia join the European Union?
questions.explanation: Croatia became an EU member state on 1 July 2013 (Hrvatska je postala članica EU 2013. godine).

questions.prompt: How do you make a formal complaint politely?
options: Nisam zadovoljan jer klimatizacija ne radi.
questions.explanation: Nisam zadovoljan/zadovoljna jer... (I am not satisfied because...) is the appropriate polite complaint opener for formal contexts like hotels.

questions.prompt: Complete the formal request: Bio ___ zahvalan ako biste mi pomogli. (I would be grateful if you could help me — male speaker.)
questions.explanation: Bio bih zahvalan = I would be grateful (male speaker). This conditional form (bih) is used for polite formal requests. Female: Bila bih zahvalna.

questions.prompt: What does ručna prtljaga mean?
questions.explanation: Ručna prtljaga = hand luggage (carry-on). Predana prtljaga = checked luggage, izgubljena prtljaga = lost luggage, pohrana prtljage = luggage storage.
